rules.reason: Mentions Allah, Salah, Quran, worship, iman, sin, or religious duty. The spec requires founder approval for religious content.
rules.notes: This is the rule that makes essentially all on-brand Tilawah Lock content approval-gated. That is the intended safety posture; the founder-approved template library (see CLAUDE.md addendum A2) is the sanctioned route to autonomy, not a loosening of this rule.

rules.reason: Discusses payment or premium features alongside worship. The spec requires founder approval for premium/paywall content tied to worship.
rules.notes: The Red counterpart (RED-WORSHIP-PAYWALL-FORCED) fires only when payment is framed as religiously obligatory. Ordinary pricing content near worship language lands here.

rules.reason: Religious emotional framing. The spec lists religious emotional content as approval-required for Tilawah Lock.
Discusses taxes or legal matters. The spec makes tax-related claims approval-required and forbids tax and legal guarantees.
Discusses brokers. The spec makes broker-related content approval-required and warns against becoming primarily anti-broker.
rules.notes: Catches unlisted broker names indirectly — the word 'broker' nearly always appears alongside one. RED-RR-BROKER-NAMED handles the named case.

rules.reason: References the Community Rate Board or rate transparency. The spec states Community Rate Board messaging requires founder approval.
Makes a freight-intelligence claim. The spec makes freight intelligence claims approval-required.
Implies a financial outcome. The spec makes financial outcome claims approval-required.
rules.notes: Deliberately fires on the number, not the verb. Cost-per-mile education without an outcome figure stays Green, which is what the spec's auto-publish allowlist intends.

rules.reason: Appears to use a real route, rate, or customer example. The spec makes real route/rate examples and real user examples approval-required.
Uses a testimonial, user comment, or user screenshot. The spec makes real user comments, testimonials, screenshots, and examples approval-required.
Compares against a competitor. The spec makes competitor comparisons approval-required.
Makes a strong or absolute claim. The spec makes strong claims approval-required.
patterns: \b(?:the only|the best|number one|#1|nobody else|no other|never fails|always works|instantly|overnight)\b

rules.reason: Contains creator outreach. The spec makes creator outreach approval-required and manual-only.
Reads as a community reply. The spec keeps community replies manual-only and approval-gated.
patterns: \b(?:great question|thanks for (?:asking|sharing)|to answer your question|as (?:someone|a dev) who built)\b
